```{r scenario-truth, include=FALSE}
scenario <- as.integer(params$scenario)
stopifnot(scenario %in% study$grid$scenario)
rho <- unique(study$grid$rho)
set_name <- corr_set("continuous", rho)
sc_row <- resolve_set(set_name)
sc_row <- sc_row[sc_row$scenario == scenario, ]

# the true modifiers, read off the scenario's te_expr (R/dgm_scenarios.R)
modifiers <- Filter(function(v) te_uses(sc_row, v), paste0("X", 1:5))
# none in scenario 1, the null
mod_label <- if (length(modifiers) > 0) paste(modifiers, collapse = ", ") else "none"

# The reference Var(tau), from one large draw of the study's own DGM rather than
# a hand-entered constant, so it follows R/dgm_scenarios.R. calib_n = the
# study's n keeps bW where the study has it; bW is additive and does not enter
# the variance either way. Monte Carlo SE on 2e5 draws is ~0.3%.
set.seed(20261011)
true_var_tau <- var(generate_scenario_data(
  scenario, 2e5, set = set_name, calib_n = unique(study$grid$n))$truth$tau)
```

## Does an interim finding survive the rest of the trial?

If a subgroup, a CATE ranking of covariates, or the spread of estimated
treatment effects looks real partway through a trial, does it still look real
once more data has accrued? This study fits three CATE estimators on the first
`interim_prop` of a simulated trial and checks whether what they find there —
top and bottom responder subgroups, the variance of the estimated CATEs, the
ranking of covariates by variable importance, and whether the single most
important covariate still interacts with treatment — replicates on the remaining
stage. It is a robustness check for CATE-based subgroup discovery, not an
estimator comparison.

This report covers **scenario `r scenario`**. The study runs scenarios 1–4; each
has its own render of this file.

### Design

| | |
|---|---|
| scenario | `r scenario` of 1–4, correlated continuous set at rho = `r rho` (see below) |
| n | 1000, one trial split into its first `n * interim_prop` participants and the rest |
| `interim_prop` | 0.25 to 0.75 in steps of 0.05 — 11 interim points |
| runs | 100 per scenario — **4400 array jobs** over the four scenarios |
| folds | DR SuperLearner only: 5 for a stage below 500 rows, else 10 |
| interaction tests | linear models, each with classical and HC3 standard errors. HC3 throughout, except the section comparing the two |

**Estimators**: `causal_forest`, `dr_random_forest` and `dr_superlearner`
(`R/cate_models.R`). The question is whether one estimator's own findings
persist across stages. The DR SuperLearner is crossfit, and its TE-VIMs come
from crossfit refits of its stage-2 SuperLearner on the same folds.

**Variable importance**: two measures, computed side by side for each estimator
in each stage (`validation/val_common.R`).

- **TE-VIM** — refit the second stage with each covariate dropped in turn and
  compare out-of-bag prediction error. Asks how much worse the CATE is predicted
  without that covariate.
- **Surrogate TreeSHAP** — fit a tuned xgboost surrogate to the estimated CATEs
  and take exact TreeSHAP of it, averaging |SHAP| over units ("Strategy 3" /
  indirect SHAP, Svensson et al.). Asks how much of each unit's estimated CATE
  is attributable to that covariate.

They need not agree, which is why both are carried: each gets its own
stage-1-vs-stage-2 rank comparison, and each nominates its own top covariate for
the interaction test below.

### What the truth is

```{r truth-text, results='asis'}
truth_text <- list(
  "1" = paste0(
    "Scenario 1 of the continuous set is `TE_10[1]`, the **null**: `tau = bW` for ",
    "everyone, so `Var(tau) = 0` and no covariate modifies the effect. X1 and X2 ",
    "are prognostic only, and X3–X5 are drawn but unused. Nothing chunk 1 finds is ",
    "real, so every significant chunk 2 interaction test - subgroup or top ",
    "covariate, any form - is a **type I error**, and every replication rate below ",
    "should sit at the nominal 5%. A rate above it is how often an interim finding ",
    "would \"validate\" when there is nothing to find. Every `true2` contrast is 0. ",
    "The parts of this report about true modifiers (ranked top, nominated) are 0 ",
    "by definition here."),
  "2" = paste0(
    "Scenario 2 of the continuous set is `TE_10[2]`: `tau = bW + b4 * X4`, with ",
    "`b4 = ", sc_row$b4, "` and `X4 ~ N(0, 1)`. X4 is the only modifier. `X3` and ",
    "`X5` are generated (every scenario draws X1–X5) but do not modify the effect. ",
    "(Before the 2026-09-26 renumbering this was scenario 3, and results produced ",
    "then sit under `scenario_3/`.)"),
  "3" = paste0(
    "Scenario 3 of the continuous set is `TE_10[3]`: ",
    "`tau = bW + b3 * X3 + b4 * X4 + b45 * X4 * X5`, with `b3 = ", sc_row$b3,
    "`, `b4 = ", sc_row$b4, "`, `b45 = ", sc_row$b45, "`, `X3 ~ Bernoulli(",
    sc_row$X3_prob, ")` and `X4`, `X5 ~ N(0, 1)`. Three modifiers. X3 is the largest single ",
    "source of the heterogeneity (`b3^2 * Var(X3)` = ",
    signif(sc_row$b3^2 * sc_row$X3_prob * (1 - sc_row$X3_prob), 2),
    ", of a total `Var(tau)` of about ", signif(true_var_tau, 2),
    "), so it is the covariate a working estimator should nominate ",
    "most often. X5 modifies the effect only through its product with X4, so its ",
    "*linear* marginal interaction is weak even though it is a true modifier.\n\n",
    "A nominated X3 is binary. Its median split is X3 itself (before 2026-10-11 ",
    "the split was `X3 > median(X3)`, all 0 for a Bernoulli(0.7), and `p_split` ",
    "was NA), and the continuous, split and both data-driven forms all test the ",
    "same 0/1 contrast."),
  "4" = paste0(
    "Scenario 4 of the continuous set is `TE_10[4]`: `tau = bW + b4 * cos(X4)`, with ",
    "`b4 = ", sc_row$b4, "` and `X4 ~ N(0, 1)`. X4 is the only modifier, but the ",
    "effect is **symmetric** in it: `cos` is even and X4 is centred on 0, so ",
    "E[tau | X4 > 0] = E[tau | X4 < 0] and the best linear fit of tau on X4 has ",
    "slope 0. The linear and median-split top-covariate tests (`p_cts`, ",
    "`p_cts_adj`, `p_split`) therefore have **no power** against it even when X4 ",
    "is correctly nominated: their rejection rate should sit near the nominal 5%. ",
    "That is a finding about those tests, not a failure of the estimators. The ",
    "data-driven forms are built to see it: the tree split (`p_dd`) can cut X4 ",
    "into middle vs. tails, and the spline projection (`p_proj`) follows the ",
    "curve. The same symmetry holds for X4's correlated proxies, whose E[tau | X] ",
    "is even too. The top-10% responders are the participants with X4 near 0 and ",
    "the bottom 10% those in the tails, which the subgroup tree can learn.")
)
cat(truth_text[[as.character(scenario)]], "\n")
```

The covariates are correlated: X1–X5 and X01–X03 come from a Gaussian copula
with exchangeable latent correlation `r rho` (`R/dgm_scenarios.R`, CORRELATED
COVARIATES), X1 and X3 thresholded to binary. X04 and X05 (a three-level
categorical) are the only covariates independent of the modifiers.

Each run is one trial of 1000, and stage 1 is its first `n * interim_prop`
participants, so a run's stage 1 at 0.25 is nested in its stage 1 at 0.30 and
curves across `interim_prop` are paired within run. The same run number draws
the same participants in every scenario; only the CATE changes.

Consequences used as reference lines below:

- **`Var(tau)` ≈ `r signif(true_var_tau, 3)`**, in both stages and at every
  `interim_prop`, computed by simulating the DGM. The copula scales the
  continuous covariates' latent columns, so their marginal distributions are
  unchanged by the correlation, and `bW` is additive, so it does not enter.
- **The true HTE drivers are: `r mod_label`.** The other covariates in the
  fitted model are noise as far as the CATE is concerned, and a working
  estimator should rank a true modifier most important in both stages, under
  either importance measure.
- **The noise covariates are not exchangeable.** Those correlated with the
  modifiers carry some of their signal, so they should rank consistently above
  X04/X05 in both stages. That structure inflates the stage-to-stage rank
  correlation without any real discovery behind it. Dropping one covariate at a
  time also lowers a modifier's TE-VIM, because its correlated proxies stand in
  for part of it.
- **A true modifier is the right answer to the top-variable test.** A run that
  nominates one and then finds a significant interaction with it in stage 2 has
  done the whole job correctly. A run that nominates a proxy will still often
  find a significant *marginal* interaction (`p_cts`), because E[tau | X] moves
  with any covariate correlated with a modifier. The adjusted test
  (`p_cts_adj`) conditions on the other covariates and should not.

```{r data}
res_path <- study$res_path
fig_path <- here("../results/all_figures/validation")
dir.create(fig_path, showWarnings = FALSE)
metrics <- readRDS(file.path(res_path, "cts_val_metrics.RDS"))

# this report's scenario only; rho takes one value. Every estimator is shown:
# causal forest, DR random forest and DR SuperLearner.
this_scenario <- function(d) {
  d %>% filter(scenario == !!scenario) %>%
    select(-any_of(c("scenario", "rho"))) %>% apply_labels()
}
subgroups_all <- this_scenario(metrics$subgroups)
variances     <- this_scenario(metrics$variances)
var_imps      <- this_scenario(metrics$var_imps)
top_var_all   <- this_scenario(metrics$top_var)

# HC3 is the primary standard error; the classical rows are only read by the
# section comparing the two
subgroups <- subgroups_all %>% filter(se == "hc3")
top_var   <- top_var_all   %>% filter(se == "hc3")

n_models <- length(unique(subgroups$model))

# interim_prop stays numeric so it can carry an axis; `interim_lab` is the short
# form for the few plots that still need one panel per interim point. Built from
# the data rather than a literal vector - there are 11 of them now, and the
# grid is free to change again.
MEASURE_LABELS <- c(tevim = "TE-VIM", shap = "TreeSHAP")
SE_LABELS <- c(classical = "Classical", hc3 = "HC3")
FORM_LABELS <- c(p_cts = "Continuous W x X",
                 p_cts_adj = "Continuous W x X, adjusted",
                 p_split = "Median split",
                 p_dd = "Data-driven split (tree)",
                 p_proj = "Spline projection")

add_interim_lab <- function(d) {
  d %>% mutate(interim_lab = factor(paste0(round(interim_prop * 100), "%"),
                                    levels = paste0(round(sort(unique(interim_prop)) * 100), "%")))
}

subgroups_all <- add_interim_lab(subgroups_all)
subgroups <- add_interim_lab(subgroups)
variances <- add_interim_lab(variances)
var_imps  <- add_interim_lab(var_imps)  %>%
  mutate(measure = label_factor(measure, MEASURE_LABELS))
top_var_all <- add_interim_lab(top_var_all) %>%
  mutate(measure = label_factor(measure, MEASURE_LABELS))
top_var   <- add_interim_lab(top_var)   %>%
  mutate(measure = label_factor(measure, MEASURE_LABELS))

n_runs_expected <- study$n_sims
n_covariates <- length(unique(var_imps$variables))

# the three interim points the study ran before the grid was refined - used to
# keep the summary tables to a readable length
landmarks <- c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)

# figure files carry the scenario, so the three renders do not overwrite each other
fig_name <- function(stem) paste0("cts_val_", stem, "_sc", scenario, ".png")
```

## Subgroup persistence

`chunk_validations()` (`validation/val_common.R`) fits a tree on stage 1's top/bottom-10%-CATE responder
groups, predicts them into stage 2, and tests the `W x subgroup` interaction
there.


```{r subgroup-long}
pivot_subgroups <- function(d) {
  d %>%
    pivot_longer(c(top_pval, bottom_pval), names_to = "which", values_to = "pval") %>%
    mutate(which = recode(which, top_pval = "Top 10%", bottom_pval = "Bottom 10%"),
           which = factor(which, levels = c("Top 10%", "Bottom 10%")))
}
subgroups_long <- pivot_subgroups(subgroups)
```

```{r subgroup-ecdf, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
ggplot(subgroups_long, aes(x = pval, colour = interim_prop, group = interim_prop)) +
  stat_ecdf(geom = "step", linewidth = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.1, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(model ~ which) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "viridis") +
  drf_theme() +
  labs(title = "Cumulative distribution of stage 2 subgroup p-values",
       x = "p-value (W x subgroup interaction)", y = "Cumulative proportion",
       colour = "Interim\nproportion")
ggsave(fig_name("sg_cumu"), path = fig_path, width = 20, height = 6 * n_models,
       units = "cm")
```

```{r subgroup-prop, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
subgroup_prop <- subgroups_long %>%
  tidyr::crossing(threshold = c(0.05, 0.1)) %>%
  mutate(is_sig = pval < threshold,
         threshold = factor(threshold, levels = c(0.05, 0.1), labels = c("0.05", "0.10"))) %>%
  group_by(model, which, interim_prop, threshold) %>%
  summarise(runs = sum(!is.na(is_sig)),
            prop_sig = mean(is_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
            mcse = sqrt(prop_sig * (1 - prop_sig) / runs),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(subgroup_prop, aes(x = interim_prop, y = prop_sig, colour = threshold,
                          ymin = prop_sig - qnorm(0.975) * mcse,
                          ymax = prop_sig + qnorm(0.975) * mcse)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(fill = threshold), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_grid(model ~ which) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(subgroup_prop$interim_prop))) +
  # 0.05 steps as before, but over the whole range: the other estimators can
  # fall below the 0.45 the DR random forest alone never went under
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.05)) +
  drf_scale() +
  scale_fill_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
  drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Proportion of successful stage 2 interaction tests",
       x = "Stage 1 proportion", y = "Proportion with p < threshold",
       colour = "Threshold", fill = "Threshold")
ggsave(fig_name("sg_props"), path = fig_path, width = 20, height = 6 * n_models,
       units = "cm")

```

## CATE variance stability

Does the spread of estimated treatment effects in stage 1 (`vt1`) match the
spread in stage 2 (`vt2`)? The dashed line is the true `Var(tau)`
(≈ `r signif(true_var_tau, 3)`).

```{r variance-box, fig.height=3.5 * n_models}
tidy_variances <- variances %>%
  rename(stage1 = vt1, stage2 = vt2) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(stage1, stage2), names_to = "stage", values_to = "variance") %>%
  mutate(stage = recode(stage, stage1 = "stage 1", stage2 = "stage 2"))

ggplot(tidy_variances, aes(x = interim_lab, y = variance, fill = stage)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = true_var_tau, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  facet_wrap(~model, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
  drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "CATE variance in early vs. late stage",
       subtitle = paste0("Dashed line: true Var(tau) = ", signif(true_var_tau, 3),
                         ". stage 1 grows and stage 2 shrinks left to right."),
       x = "Interim proportion", y = "Variance of estimated CATE", fill = "stage")
```

```{r variance-scatter, fig.height=9}
ggplot(variances, aes(x = vt1, y = vt2, colour = model)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~interim_lab, ncol = 4) +
  drf_scale() +
  drf_theme() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  labs(title = "CATE variance, stage 1 vs. stage 2, per run",
       subtitle = "Dashed line: vt1 = vt2 (perfect replication)",
       x = "Variance in stage 1", y = "Variance in stage 2") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r variance-change}
var_change_summary <- variances %>%
  group_by(model, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(runs = sum(!is.na(var_change)),
            mean_change = mean(var_change, na.rm = TRUE),
            mcse = sd(var_change, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(runs),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(var_change_summary, aes(x = interim_prop, y = mean_change, colour = model,
                               ymin = mean_change - qnorm(0.975) * mcse,
                               ymax = mean_change + qnorm(0.975) * mcse)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(fill = model), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(var_change_summary$interim_prop))) +
  drf_scale() +
  scale_fill_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
  drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Mean change in CATE variance, stage 2 minus stage 1",
       x = "Interim proportion", y = "Mean(vt2 - vt1)",
       colour = "Model", fill = "Model")
```

## Variable-importance rank stability

`chunk_validations()` ranks each covariate's importance within a stage via
`rank()`: **rank 1 is the least important covariate, rank `r n_covariates`
is the most important.** `r if (length(modifiers) > 0) paste0("The true HTE drivers are ", mod_label, ", so a working estimator should rank one of them ", n_covariates, " (most important) in both stages, under both measures.") else "Scenario 1 has no HTE drivers, so no ranking is right: these plots show how stable a ranking of noise looks, and the proportions of runs ranking a true driver top are 0 by definition."`

```{r rank-agreement, fig.height=5}
rank_corr <- var_imps %>%
  group_by(model, measure, interim_prop, run) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  summarise(rho = cor(vi1, vi2, method = "spearman"), .groups = "drop")

rank_corr_summary <- rank_corr %>%
  group_by(model, measure, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(runs = sum(!is.na(rho)),
            mean_rho = mean(rho, na.rm = TRUE),
            mcse = sd(rho, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(runs),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(rank_corr_summary, aes(x = interim_prop, y = mean_rho, colour = measure,
                              ymin = mean_rho - qnorm(0.975) * mcse,
                              ymax = mean_rho + qnorm(0.975) * mcse)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(fill = measure), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(rank_corr_summary$interim_prop))) +
  drf_scale() +
  scale_fill_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
  drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Spearman correlation between stage 1 and stage 2 importance ranks",
       x = "Interim proportion", y = "Mean Spearman correlation between stages",
       colour = "Measure", fill = "Measure")
```

```{r rank-mean, fig.height=3.5 * n_models}
mean_vi <- var_imps %>%
  group_by(variables, model, measure, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(mean_vi1 = mean(vi1, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_vi2 = mean(vi2, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(mean_vi1, mean_vi2), names_to = "stage", values_to = "mean_rank") %>%
  mutate(stage = recode(stage, mean_vi1 = "Stage 1", mean_vi2 = "Stage 2"))

ggplot(mean_vi, aes(x = interim_prop, y = mean_rank, colour = variables,
                    linetype = stage)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(model ~ measure) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(mean_vi$interim_prop))) +
  scale_colour_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
  drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Mean importance rank per covariate, by stage",
       subtitle = paste0("Rank 1 = least important, ", n_covariates,
                         " = most important. True HTE drivers: ", mod_label, "."),
       x = "Interim proportion", y = "Mean rank",
       colour = "Covariate", linetype = "stage")
```

```{r rank-change, fig.height=3.5 * n_models}
top_vars <- var_imps %>%
  group_by(variables, model, measure, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(mean_abs_change = mean(abs(diff), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(top_vars, aes(x = interim_prop, y = mean_abs_change, colour = variables)) +

  facet_grid(model ~ measure) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(top_vars$interim_prop))) +

```

```{r modifier-top, fig.height=5}
modifier_top <- var_imps %>%
  group_by(model, measure, interim_prop, run) %>%
  summarise(top1 = variables[which.max(vi1)] %in% modifiers,
            top2 = variables[which.max(vi2)] %in% modifiers,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(model, measure, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(runs = n(),
            p_top_stage1 = mean(top1),
            p_top_stage2 = mean(top2),
            p_top_both = mean(top1 & top2),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(modifier_top, aes(x = interim_prop, y = p_top_both, colour = measure)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(modifier_top$interim_prop))) +
  ylim(0, 1) +
  drf_scale() +
  drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
  labs(title = paste0("How often a true HTE driver (", mod_label,
                      ") is ranked most important in both stages"),
       x = "Interim proportion", y = "Proportion of runs", colour = "Measure")
```

```{r modifier-top-table}
kable(modifier_top %>% filter(interim_prop %in% landmarks), digits = 3,

                    "Modifier top in both"),

                       ") is ranked most important, at the three landmark interim points"))
```

## Does the top-ranked driver replicate?

The point of ranking covariates is whether the winner means anything. For each
estimator and each importance measure, `chunk_validations()` takes stage 1's
most important covariate and tests its treatment interaction on the remaining
trial participants — five ways:

- `p_cts`, the continuous `W x X_top` interaction;
- `p_cts_adj`, the `W:X_top` coefficient of `Y ~ W * (all covariates)`, i.e. the
  same interaction holding the other covariates fixed;
- `p_split`, the marginal test after dichotomising `X_top` at its stage-2
  median (a binary `X_top` is its own split);
- `p_dd`, a **data-driven split**: a depth-2 regression tree of stage 1's
  estimated CATE on `X_top` alone, its leaves grouped into above / below stage
  1's mean CATE, and that split carried into stage 2. It can be one threshold,
  a binary covariate's 0/1, or middle vs. tails;
- `p_proj`, a **spline projection**: a smoothing spline (4 df) of stage 1's
  estimated CATE on `X_top`, evaluated at stage 2's `X_top` and tested as a
  1-df `W x g(X_top)` interaction.

Only stage 1 decides the shape of the two data-driven tests, so each is still
an honest test in stage 2.

```{r top-var-long}
pivot_top_var <- function(d) {
  d %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(names(FORM_LABELS)), names_to = "form", values_to = "pval") %>%
    mutate(form = label_factor(form, FORM_LABELS))
}
top_var_long <- pivot_top_var(top_var)

top_var_prop <- top_var_long %>%
  mutate(is_sig = pval < 0.05) %>%
  group_by(model, measure, form, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(runs = sum(!is.na(is_sig)),
            prop_sig = mean(is_sig, na.rm = TRUE),
            mcse = sqrt(prop_sig * (1 - prop_sig) / runs),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r top-var-prop, fig.height=14}
ggplot(top_var_prop, aes(x = interim_prop, y = prop_sig, colour = model,
                         ymin = prop_sig - qnorm(0.975) * mcse,
                         ymax = prop_sig + qnorm(0.975) * mcse)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(fill = model), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_grid(form ~ measure) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(top_var_prop$interim_prop))) +
  # coord_cartesian, not ylim(): ylim() drops any ribbon that pokes past 0 or 1
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  drf_scale() +
  scale_fill_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
  drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Proportion of runs where the interim's top covariate still interacts in stage 2",
       subtitle = "Ribbon: 95% Monte Carlo interval. Dashed line: nominal 5%.",
       x = "Interim proportion", y = "Proportion with p < 0.05",
       colour = "Model", fill = "Model")
ggsave(fig_name("topvar_props"), path = fig_path, width = 20, height = 30, units = "cm")
```

The median split throws away information, so the gap between the continuous and
median-split panels is the cost of dichotomising a discovered driver rather
than testing it as it stands. The gap between the continuous and adjusted
panels is mostly how much of the "replication" comes from nominating a proxy
of a modifier that interacts with treatment only through its correlation with
it — partly, too, the power that adjusting for correlated covariates costs when
a modifier itself is nominated. The data-driven panels show what is gained when
the shape of the test is learned rather than assumed; where the modifier is
monotone they should track the continuous and median-split forms.

```{r dd-cuts}
# the cuts and the high-side share do not depend on the standard errors, so the
# HC3 rows alone carry them
dd_summary <- top_var %>%
  filter(interim_prop %in% landmarks) %>%
  mutate(n_cuts = ifelse(dd_cuts == "", 0L, lengths(strsplit(dd_cuts, ";")))) %>%
  group_by(model, measure, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(runs = n(),
            nominates_modifier = mean(x_top %in% modifiers),
            no_split = mean(n_cuts == 0),
            one_cut = mean(n_cuts == 1),
            two_plus_cuts = mean(n_cuts >= 2),
            mean_high_share = mean(dd_prop),
            .groups = "drop")

kable(dd_summary, digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Model", "Measure", "Interim point", "Runs", "Nominates a modifier",
                    "No split", "One cut", "Two or more cuts", "Mean stage 2 share high"),
      caption = paste("The data-driven split at the three landmark interim points.",
                      "Two or more cuts is a middle-vs-tails or banded split;",
                      "'share high' is the stage 2 share on the high-CATE side."))
```

```{r top-var-agreement}
top_var_agree <- top_var %>%
  group_by(model, measure, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(runs = n(),
            p_x_top_is_modifier = mean(x_top %in% modifiers),
            p_stages_agree = mean(x_top == x_top2),

ggplot(top_var_agree, aes(x = interim_prop, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p_x_top_is_modifier, linetype = "Nominates a modifier")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p_stages_agree, linetype = "stages agree")) +
```

```{r top-var-table}
      col.names = c("Model", "Measure", "Interim point", "Runs",
                    "Nominates a modifier", "stages agree"),
```

## Direction of the replications

A significant chunk 2 test only counts as a replication if the effect goes the
way chunk 1 said it would. Since 2026-10-12 every interaction test saves its
`W:v` estimate (`est`) next to its p-value, and two reference contrasts on the
same scale (`validation/val_common.R`, "Reference contrasts"):

- `ref1`: the same contrast computed on stage 1's *estimated* CATE, i.e. the
  direction (and size) stage 1 implied. It is positive for the top 10%,
  negative for the bottom 10%, and positive for the data-driven split, by
  construction.
- `true2`: the same contrast computed on stage 2's *true* CATE, i.e. what the
  stage 2 test is estimating. It is 0 in scenario 1.

A significant test whose `est` has the sign of `ref1` replicated stage 1's
claim. One whose `est` has the sign of `true2` also points the right way in
truth. Where `true2` is 0 (scenario 1) the truth has no direction, and only
the stage 1 comparison is shown. HC3 standard errors.

```{r direction-long}
# est / ref1 / true2 and the p-value of every test, one row per run x test.
# est, ref1 and true2 are the same under both kinds of standard error, so the
# HC3 rows alone carry them
DIR_PATTERN <- "^(p|est|ref1|true2)_(.+)$"

direction_long <- bind_rows(
  subgroups %>%
    rename(p_top = top_pval, p_bottom = bottom_pval) %>%
    select(model, interim_prop, run, matches(DIR_PATTERN)) %>%
    pivot_longer(matches(DIR_PATTERN), names_to = c(".value", "test"),
                 names_pattern = DIR_PATTERN) %>%
    mutate(family = "Subgroup",
           test = recode(test, top = "Top 10%", bottom = "Bottom 10%"),
           measure = "-"),
  top_var %>%
    select(model, measure, interim_prop, run, matches(DIR_PATTERN)) %>%
    pivot_longer(matches(DIR_PATTERN), names_to = c(".value", "test"),
                 names_pattern = DIR_PATTERN) %>%
    mutate(family = "Top covariate",
           test = unname(FORM_LABELS[paste0("p_", test)]),
           measure = as.character(measure))
) %>%
  # a true2 within rounding of 0 has no direction (scenario 1, or a test whose
  # v carries no true signal)
  mutate(sig = p < 0.05,
         with_ref1 = sign(est) == sign(ref1),
         with_truth = ifelse(abs(true2) < 1e-8, NA, sign(est) == sign(true2)))

direction <- direction_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(p)) %>%
  group_by(family, model, measure, test, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(runs = n(),
            prop_sig = mean(sig),
            # replication rates that also require the right direction
            prop_sig_ref1 = mean(sig & with_ref1, na.rm = TRUE),
            prop_sig_truth = if (all(is.na(with_truth))) NA_real_ else
              mean(sig & with_truth, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_ref1 = mean(ref1, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_est = mean(est, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_true2 = mean(true2, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

direction_rates_long <- direction %>%
  select(family, model, measure, test, interim_prop,
         prop_sig, prop_sig_ref1, prop_sig_truth) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(prop_sig, prop_sig_ref1, prop_sig_truth),
               names_to = "rate", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  mutate(rate = factor(rate, levels = c("prop_sig", "prop_sig_ref1", "prop_sig_truth"),
                       labels = c("p < 0.05", "p < 0.05, stage 1's direction",
                                  "p < 0.05, true direction")))

plot_direction_rates <- function(d, facets, title) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = interim_prop, y = value, colour = rate)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 1) +
    facets +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(d$interim_prop))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    drf_scale() +
    drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
    labs(title = title,
         subtitle = paste("A gap between the lines is runs that 'replicated' in the",
                          "wrong direction. Dashed line: nominal 5%."),
         x = "Interim proportion", y = "Proportion of runs", colour = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

```{r direction-subgroups, fig.height=3.5 * n_models}
plot_direction_rates(direction_rates_long %>% filter(family == "Subgroup"),
                     facet_grid(model ~ test),
                     "Subgroup replications, and how many went the right way")
ggsave(fig_name("sg_direction"), path = fig_path, width = 20, height = 6 * n_models,
       units = "cm")
```

```{r direction-topvar, fig.height=14}
for (m in sort(unique(direction$model))) {
  print(plot_direction_rates(
    direction_rates_long %>% filter(family == "Top covariate", model == m),
    facet_grid(test ~ measure),
    paste0("Top-covariate replications, and how many went the right way: ", m)))
}
```

Stage 1's own contrast (`ref1`) against what stage 2 estimates (`est`) and the
truth there (`true2`), averaged over runs. `ref1` well above `true2` is
stage 1 overstating its finding (a winner's curse). `est` tracks `true2`,
because the stage 2 test estimates it without bias.

```{r direction-shrinkage, fig.height=3.5 * n_models}
direction %>%
  filter(family == "Subgroup") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(mean_ref1, mean_est, mean_true2), names_to = "quantity",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(quantity = factor(quantity, levels = c("mean_ref1", "mean_est", "mean_true2"),
                           labels = c("Stage 1 claim (ref1)", "Stage 2 estimate (est)",
                                      "Stage 2 truth (true2)"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = interim_prop, y = value, colour = quantity)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  facet_grid(model ~ test) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(direction$interim_prop))) +
  drf_scale() +
  drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Subgroup contrast: stage 1's claim, stage 2's estimate and the truth",
       subtitle = "Difference in treatment effect, subgroup minus the rest; mean over runs",
       x = "Interim proportion", y = "Contrast", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r direction-table}
kable(direction %>%
        filter(interim_prop %in% landmarks) %>%
        select(family, test, measure, model, interim_prop, runs, prop_sig,
               prop_sig_ref1, prop_sig_truth, mean_ref1, mean_est, mean_true2) %>%
        arrange(family, test, measure, model, interim_prop),
      digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Test", "Form", "Measure", "Model", "Interim point", "Runs",
                    "p < 0.05", "... stage 1's direction", "... true direction",
                    "Mean ref1", "Mean est", "Mean true2"),
      caption = paste("Replication with and without the direction, at the three",
                      "landmark interim points, HC3. 'True direction' is blank where",
                      "the truth has none (scenario 1)."))
```

## Classical vs. HC3 standard errors

Every interaction test above was also run with classical standard errors. The
noise is homoskedastic, but `Y ~ W * v` leaves out the prognostic X1 and X2 and
the spread of tau within each level of `v`, so the residual variance differs
across the `W x v` cells — most where `v` is a small (10%) responder subgroup.
HC3 is the cell-wise variance there; the classical pooled variance comes almost
entirely from the large cells.

```{r se-compare, fig.height=3.5 * n_models}
se_rates <- bind_rows(
  pivot_subgroups(subgroups_all) %>%
    transmute(model, se, interim_prop, test = paste("Subgroup:", which), pval),
  pivot_top_var(top_var_all) %>%
    transmute(model, se, interim_prop,
              test = paste0("Top covariate (", measure, "): ", form), pval)
) %>%
  group_by(model, se, test, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(prop_sig = mean(pval < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(se = label_factor(se, SE_LABELS))

ggplot(se_rates %>% filter(grepl("^Subgroup", test)),
       aes(x = interim_prop, y = prop_sig, colour = se)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_grid(model ~ test) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(se_rates$interim_prop))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  drf_scale() +
  drf_theme(rotate_x = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Subgroup tests: proportion with p < 0.05, classical vs. HC3",
       x = "Interim proportion", y = "Proportion with p < 0.05", colour = "Standard errors")
```

```{r se-compare-table}
se_table <- se_rates %>%
  filter(interim_prop %in% landmarks) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = se, values_from = prop_sig) %>%
  mutate(difference = HC3 - Classical) %>%
  arrange(test, model, interim_prop)

kable(se_table, digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Model", "Test", "Interim point", "Classical", "HC3", "HC3 - classical"),
      caption = paste("Proportion with p < 0.05 under each kind of standard error,",
                      "every test, at the three landmark interim points"))
```

## Headline table

At the three landmark interim points, to keep it readable — every panel above
carries all eleven. HC3 standard errors.

```{r headline-table}
# `runs` is counted per subgroup and the two can differ (interaction_pval
# returns NA more often for bottom10), so it is joined on separately rather than
# carried through the pivot, where it would split each cell into two rows.
runs_per_cell <- subgroups %>%
  group_by(model, interim_prop) %>%
  summarise(runs = n(), .groups = "drop")

# subgroup_prop carries both thresholds; the table reports p < 0.05, as every
# other column does - pivoting both would make each cell a list
headline <- subgroup_prop %>%
  filter(interim_prop %in% landmarks, threshold == "0.05") %>%
  select(model, which, interim_prop, prop_sig) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = which, values_from = prop_sig, names_prefix = "sig_") %>%
  left_join(runs_per_cell, by = c("model", "interim_prop")) %>%
  relocate(runs, .after = interim_prop) %>%
  left_join(variances %>% group_by(model, interim_prop) %>%
              summarise(mean_vt1 = mean(vt1, na.rm = TRUE),
                       mean_vt2 = mean(vt2, na.rm = TRUE),
                       .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("model", "interim_prop")) %>%
  left_join(var_change_summary %>% select(model, interim_prop, mean_change),
            by = c("model", "interim_prop")) %>%
  left_join(rank_corr_summary %>%
              select(model, measure, interim_prop, mean_rho) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = mean_rho,
                          names_prefix = "rho_"),
            by = c("model", "interim_prop")) %>%
  left_join(top_var_prop %>%
              filter(form %in% FORM_LABELS[c("p_cts", "p_dd", "p_proj")]) %>%
              mutate(form = recode(as.character(form),
                                   !!!setNames(c("cts", "dd", "proj"),
                                               FORM_LABELS[c("p_cts", "p_dd", "p_proj")]))) %>%
              select(model, measure, form, interim_prop, prop_sig) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = c(form, measure), values_from = prop_sig,
                          names_prefix = "topvar_"),
            by = c("model", "interim_prop")) %>%
  arrange(model, interim_prop)

kable(headline, digits = 3,
      caption = paste("Landmark summary. sig_* = proportion of runs where that",
                      "subgroup validates; rho_* = mean rank correlation between",
                      "stages; topvar_(form)_(measure) = proportion where the",
                      "nominated top covariate still interacts, by the continuous",
                      "(cts), data-driven split (dd) and spline projection (proj)",
                      "forms."))
```
